title: Coaching, Feedback and Developing Others
summary: How to use coaching conversations and timely, specific feedback to develop supervisors' judgement and capability, and to build a strong feedback culture in the team.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: How to use coaching conversations and timely, specific feedback to develop supervisors' judgement and capability, and to build a strong feedback culture in the team.
Learning Objectives: Apply a structured coaching model in everyday management
Give feedback that is specific, balanced and actionable
Plan the development of team members' supervisory skills
Syllabus: Giving and receiving feedback, including upward feedback
Developing judgement: reviewing work without rewriting it
Intended Audience: Supervisors newly promoted, or preparing for promotion, into team leader and manager roles
Managers and heads of department in supervisory authorities seeking to strengthen their leadership
Technical specialists who lead projects, thematic reviews or cross-functional teams
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience in a supervisory or technical role is helpful. No prior management training is required.
Core Reading: Amy C. Edmondson, The Fearless Organization: Creating Psychological Safety in the Workplace (2018)
Patrick Lencioni, The Five Dysfunctions of a Team (2002)
IMF, The Making of Good Supervision: Learning to Say "No" (Staff Position Note SPN/10/08, 2010)
